title: The AI Cold War: Pax Silica vs WAICO, Explained (Stanford Tech Review, Priya Raman, Aug 15, 2026)
notes: Stanford Tech Review (independent, not Stanford-affiliated), Priya Raman, 2026-08-15. Pax Silica: US init 2025-12-12, 7 signatories (Aus/Israel/Japan/Korea/Singapore/UK/US), State Dept Jacob Helberg, physical/supply-chain, $250M consortium, grew to 24 in 6 mo. WAICO: proposed Li Qiang 2025-07, Xi APEC 2025-10, created 2026-07-16, 29 founding signatories, Shanghai HQ, Global South-oriented, Guterres attended, governance/norms. Analogy holds (bloc-building, semiconductor chokepoints, alignment pressure) but breaks (asymmetry: non-binding declaration vs treaty org; grey majority; software flowing opposite to chips - Chinese open models <10%->~40% of US-company tokens mid-2025->mid-2026). Gibney (Nature): WAICO likely unenforceable. Verdict: direction right, mechanism wrong. Data from Wikipedia as of 2026-08-15.
